decision_reason: The assigned repository is an API integration-reference bundle (WSDL/XSD, example request/response text, and documentation) for the live Bolsa de Documentos service; it does not contain the deployed API implementation or a separately versioned software client. Reject this URL as a software product source, while preserving the fact that the government service itself is live and notable.

government_provenance.note: ARTE's official page identifies Bolsa de Documentos as its live platform, and the assigned repo title says it is for that service's API; I found no official source linking this particular repository to the service implementation or naming its API contract as an official distribution.

public_source.note: The repository exposes WSDL/XSD contracts, documentation, examples, and some sample snippets, but no server/API implementation or standalone client package. It is not a public canonical source for the live service software.

eligible_license.note: The repository carries the exact EUPL-1.2 text, an OSI-approved license; it covers the repository's first-party integration examples and documentation, but does not establish the license of the absent deployed server implementation.

primary_evidence.note: Official evidence documents the operational Bolsa de Documentos service, not an independently distributed software product in this repository. No versioned client release or deployable implementation is present here.

product_identity: Bolsa de Documentos API integration-reference repository (WSDL/XSD contracts, sample messages/code, and technical documentation; no backend implementation)
agency: ARTE manages the live Bolsa de Documentos platform; sponsorship of this specific documentation repository is not independently established
license: EUPL-1.2 for first-party repository examples and documentation; not evidence for the service backend
status_note: The service itself is currently described by gov.pt and Mosaico as an ARTE platform. The assigned repository's earliest client examples and EUPL notice are from 2021; that year describes licensed example material only, not public release of the deployed API implementation. No product-wide license or source attribution is inferred.

decision_reason: The exact project is an instructional web-accessibility course collection, not an independently usable software product. The repository is mainly Jekyll course Markdown and a copied static-site theme; its MIT file retains the theme authors' 2022 copyright and does not clearly license the newly authored course material. No separately documented government software service or tool is present to catalog.

government_provenance.note: The course content commits are attributed to an author labeled ARTE, but I found no independent official ARTE/Mosaico publication page confirming the specific course collection's sponsorship or operational role; repository ownership alone is not treated as proof.

public_source.note: The public tree exposes course content and static-site template configuration, not source code for an independently identified government software tool.

eligible_license.note: The MIT notice is the Just-the-Docs theme license and retains its 2022 theme copyright. It does not expressly establish an eligible grant over ARTE-authored course content or a software product.

primary_evidence.note: The hosted pages describe twelve accessibility courses and learning materials, not a government software product. No official product listing, release, or documented operational use of software was found.

product_identity: Coleção A11Y, a Jekyll-published collection of web-accessibility training materials and courses
agency: ARTE is named in Git commit author metadata; the specific collection's formal sponsor remains unconfirmed
license: Repository contains the Just-the-Docs theme's MIT license; grant over the course content is unresolved
status_note: The repository was initialized in July 2026 and its source site contains substantive course content, but source/repo dates do not resolve the content's rights. Rejected from this software ledger as educational content rather than software; no catalog entry proposed.

public_source.note: The public tree consists of manuals, architecture material, SOAP/WSDL and XML examples; no functional software implementation is present.

eligible_license.note: An EUPL-1.2 license text is present for repository material, but the functional kit/portal implementation is absent, so scope over the software product cannot be established.

primary_evidence.note: The government portal is currently the successor to ePortugal, but no current product-specific source, release, or deployment evidence ties this documentation-only repository to software presently distributed or used as a standalone tool.

product_identity: ePortugal reserved-area generic entity-integration kit technical documentation and SOAP examples (implementation not in this repository)
agency: Agência para a Modernização Administrativa (AMA, now ARTE) for the documented kit

decision_reason: The public repository contains an actively updated client-side GitReports tool for producing audit reports from GitHub issues; the README and MIT copyright identify AMA/ARTE as developer and intended Selo de Usabilidade e Acessibilidade use. However, I found no current official page, deployed service, tagged/versioned release, or other primary evidence that this exact tool is distributed or used operationally. Hold pending product-specific notability/use evidence rather than treating the README's `Version 1.0` heading as a formal release.

government_provenance.note: The project README identifies the tool as developed by ARTE's Núcleo de Experiência e Usabilidade, and the root MIT notice names AMA (now ARTE) as copyright holder for the exact GitReports source.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the JavaScript/HTML/CSS client app and a README explaining its configuration and operation.

eligible_license.note: The exact root license is standard MIT and covers the first-party GitReports client code, subject to its notice and disclaimer conditions.

primary_evidence.note: ARTE's 2026 page confirms the current official Selo program, but does not mention or link GitReports. The tool README describes intended use, yet the repository has no tags or published releases and no independent deployment/use evidence was found.

product_identity: GitReports, a client-side HTML/JavaScript tool for generating Selo de Usabilidade e Acessibilidade audit reports from GitHub issue repositories
agency: Agência para a Modernização Administrativa (AMA, now ARTE), Núcleo de Experiência e Usabilidade
license: MIT for first-party HTML/CSS/JavaScript report-generator source
status_note: MIT was present in the initial 2025-08-19 commit, while functional report-generator source first appeared 2025-08-23; count 2025 as the first public licensed functional source. Source activity continued through 2026-04-21. No GitHub tags/releases were present; the README's internal version label is not treated as a formal release.

decision_reason: This is a real, reusable Portuguese uData theme/plugin, not the entire open-data portal. The public source and exact AGPL-3.0 grant are evidenced, and setup metadata names AMA as author. But the repository's last source activity and latest versioned release are from August 2022; the current official portal reports a newer uData 15.0.0 engine and does not identify this old theme as its current deployment. Hold pending current product-specific use/support evidence under the freshness baseline.

government_provenance.note: First-party package metadata names AMA as author and points to dados.gov.pt; its README identifies this exact package as the official Portuguese uData theme and describes the portal integration.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the uData theme/plugin package, application customization code, setup metadata, tests, and release history.

eligible_license.note: The exact root grant is GNU AGPL version 3, an OSI-approved license, for the first-party theme/plugin source. The linked documentation submodule is a separate repository and is not assumed to inherit this license.

primary_evidence.note: The official portal is current and names an open-source uData 15.0.0 engine, but does not document using this repository's older `gouvpt` theme. The candidate's v2.7.1 release and last source changes are from 2022, beyond the ordinary 24-month activity window.

product_identity: gouvpt, a Portuguese-language uData theme and extension package (including portal customizations/plugins), not the dados.gov.pt portal itself
agency: Agência para a Modernização Administrativa (AMA, now ARTE)
license: GNU AGPL-3.0 for first-party theme/plugin code; linked docs submodule has a separate scope

The latest release tag v2.7.1/source update is from 2022-08. Current portal evidence confirms the service, not continued deployment of this theme; no catalog duplicate was found.
